title: My AFLCA 2025 award: gratitude, African ambition and the work ahead
excerpt: Receiving the Outstanding Entrepreneur of the Year Award is a milestone I treasure—and an encouragement to keep building useful AI and digital systems from Africa.
author: Anzolo Kpazhi Hope

paragraphs: If you are building something useful and wondering whether anyone sees the effort behind it, I want to speak to you first. The hours spent understanding a problem, correcting a failed idea and helping someone use what you have built do not always attract applause. They still matter.

I am deeply grateful to have received the Outstanding Entrepreneur of the Year Award at the Africa Future Leadership Conference & Awards 10.0, held on 25 October 2025 at Pistis Hub in Maryland, Ikeja, Lagos. This is a moment I am proud to share with you. I receive the recognition with appreciation for the people who made it possible and a renewed sense of responsibility for the work ahead.

sections.heading: Thank you for seeing the work
paragraphs: To the AFLCA organisers, convener Ambassador Mark Idiahi and everyone who contributed to the occasion: thank you for making room for African builders and for recognising my contribution. It means a great deal to be acknowledged by a platform that brings leadership, enterprise and innovation into the same conversation.

In its Instagram announcement on 6 October 2025, @flconference named me as an award recipient and connected the recognition to my work through ECHUKU, GlemVNT and Falzz AI. I appreciate that connection. Behind the technology is a question that continues to guide me: how can the person using this system become more capable?
The original announcement is linked here so you can read the organiser’s words in their own setting. My reflection today looks forward from that 2025 milestone.

sections.heading: Honoured to belong to a wider African story
paragraphs: I also want to celebrate Oluebube Princess Amadi, reported by New Telegraph as the Tech Icon of the Year recipient at AFLCA 10.0. Seeing software and open-source engineering recognised within this wider leadership conversation is encouraging. Congratulations to her and to every fellow honouree whose work gave the occasion its meaning.

I honour earlier recipients too, including Dr Gregory Azemobor, whose entrepreneurship and philanthropy recognition was reported by Africa Future Leadership Magazine in 2024. Our work takes different forms, but I value being part of a continuing tradition of recognising African contribution.

The conference’s own account of its 2024 edition also records speakers including Dr Lucy Surhyel Newman, Charles O’Tudor and Ali Baba. I appreciate the breadth of experience such a platform brings together. These are acknowledgements of its wider history, across different editions and roles; my own award belongs to the 2025 edition.
To me, sharing in that tradition is an honour. It invites me to learn from others while bringing my own discipline, questions and work to the conversation.

sections.heading: What this means for my work in AI
paragraphs: The award recognises entrepreneurship. For me, it is also encouragement for the direction of my work as an AI and digital systems architect: building useful systems, helping people understand them and taking responsibility for how they are used.

Through ECHUKU, I want to make technology connect more clearly to everyday work. My KONTA ERP/POS project direction concerns understandable records for sales, stock and operations. My DZEVA direction concerns making AI workflows more approachable. Those are the directions I am pursuing today; the award announcement records an earlier point in that journey.

If you run a business, you deserve more than a confident demonstration. You deserve to know what a system can do, what still requires your judgement and what happens when something goes wrong. That is the standard I want my leadership in AI to serve.

If you are an engineer, start with the person who will depend on your work. Ask them to show you one recurring difficulty. Write down what a useful outcome would look like. Build a small version, test it under the conditions they actually face and record what still fails. That discipline gives ambition something solid to stand on.

sections.heading: To the builders whose names are not on a plaque
paragraphs: To every software developer, software engineer and AI engineer doing careful work across Africa: thank you. To the person maintaining a system, reviewing someone else’s code, documenting a difficult process or patiently teaching a beginner: your contribution deserves appreciation too.

If recognition has not reached you yet, I hope you will keep a record of the problems you solve. Explain your decisions. Credit the people who help you. Share what you can responsibly share, and protect the information entrusted to you. Help another builder understand something that once confused you.

An award gives us a moment to celebrate. The habits behind useful work give that celebration substance. I want to use this moment to make more room for the people whose discipline is easy to overlook.

sections.heading: Building from Africa, with global ambition
paragraphs: I believe we can build from Africa with confidence and contribute at global standards. Our languages, businesses and communities give us important problems to understand. Taking them seriously should strengthen the quality of what we create.

For me, that ambition means reliable software, honest evaluation, respect for people’s information and products that make sense in the setting where they are used. It means being willing to improve a system after the applause has ended.

Thank you to AFLCA for this recognition, to fellow builders for your contribution and to you for taking time to read my story. I hope you leave with encouragement to keep building—and with a practical question: whose work can you make easier this week?

takeaway: Choose one person your work should serve. Listen to the difficulty they face, make one useful improvement and document what you learn. I would be glad to hear what you are building.
